name: Ngwevu
sum: Ngwevu is a massospondylid sauropodomorph from the Early Jurassic Elliot Formation of South Africa, known from a single skull-bearing specimen once assigned to Massospondylus.
wsnote: No body-size figure was read in the sources consulted; the holotype was an adult about 10 years old.
holotype: BP/1/4779, found in 1978 by J. W. Kitching at Tevrede Farm, Fouriesburg district, South Africa; held at the University of the Witwatersrand.
biology: Histology shows that the holotype was an adult about 10 years old when it fossilised. A broad palate and short snout may have given it a stronger bite than Massospondylus carinatus, which could suggest niche partitioning between the two.
author: Chapelle et al. 2019
